messages.subject: equivalent of lines()?
parts:
Hi,
I have a dataset that has structure like this:

position coverage shared fixed Aprivate Bprivate
1 32420 0.001048735 0.006971006 0.008389883 0.008821715
50001 24704 0.001862047 0.009634067 0.010929404 0.004209845
100001 34522 0.005532704 0.006604484 0.0235502 0.013469672
150001 18757 0.000373194 0.008103641 0.011249134 0.006344298
200001 8045 0.002734618 0.005344935 0.011684276 0.017277812
250001 18104 0.004639859 0.001601856 0.014195758 0.007456916
300001 17378 0.001035792 0.000632984 0.014328461 0.007020371
350001 40648 0.002460146 0.001279276 0.018229679 0.013604605
400001 16565 0.001931784 0.003682463 0.019197102 0.010745548
etc.

I want to be able to do the ggplot equivalent of the basic R plot
functions: plot(position, shared) followed by lines(position, fixed)
for a number of variables such that the X axis remains as "position"
but I can add the data from the other columns as necessary to one
figure.

I'm just making the transition from qplot to ggplot now, and am having
some beginner's trouble with the syntax.
Thanks for the help.

messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Re: equivalent of lines()?
parts:
I'm guessing that position is being treated as a factor, in which case
this will work:
ggplot(
a
)+
geom_point(
aes(x=position,y=shared)
)+geom_line(
aes(x=as.numeric(position),y=fixed)
)


That will still work if position is not being treated as a factor, but
in that case this is less typing:

ggplot(
a
aes(x=position)
)+
geom_point(
aes(y=shared)
)+geom_line(
aes(y=fixed)
)

parts:
You can also plot them all at once by transforming the data:

library(ggplot2)
dm <- melt(d, id = "fixed")
qplot(fixed, value, data = dm, colour = variable) +
geom_line() + scale_y_log10()
